analysis.location_and_population: United States; globally referenced for human rabies burden. Affected populations include children under 15, pet owners, veterinary professionals, and wildlife (bats, raccoons, foxes).
analysis.event: Guidance article on rabies public health impacts, vaccination, and exposure management published by the American Animal Hospital Association (AAHA). It synthesizes veterinary expertise, CDC data, and jurisdictional vaccination laws to address rabies prevention and control.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Globally, at least 70,000 human rabies deaths annually; 40% occur in children under 15, and 99% result from dog bites. analysis.brief_en: The American Animal Hospital Association (AAHA) published guidance on 24 August 2026 outlining the ongoing public-health burden of rabies, with at least 70,000 global deaths annually—40% in children under 15 and 99% from dog bites. In the U.S., 17 human cases were recorded from 2015–2024, while wildlife such as bats, raccoons, and foxes are ten times more likely to carry rabies than domestic animals; cats are four times more likely than dogs. Post-exposure prophylaxis in the U.S. is most often prompted by cat exposures. The article highlights jurisdictional disparities in rabies vaccination laws, with only 39 states mandating dog vaccination and fewer for cats and ferrets, alongside challenges exacerbated by COVID-19 including vaccine hesitancy, reduced surveillance, and strained healthcare access. AAHA’s 2025 One Health guidelines urge closer collaboration between veterinary and human medicine to strengthen prevention and control.
